texts.preamble: Sameer Khan And Another vs State Of U.P. on 27 March, 2023 High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad ?Court No. - 88 Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 10754 of 2023 Applicant :- Sameer Khan And Another Opposite Party :- State of U.P. Counsel for Applicant :- Lakshman Tripathi,Aniruddha Ojha
texts.facts: The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 301 of 2022, under Sections 188, 273 IPC & 5/15 of Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 & 3/63 of Food Safety and Standard Authority Act, 2006, Police Station Sigra, District Varanasi, during pendency of the trial in the court below. FIR of the present case was lodged against the applicant and two others and according to the FIR, from the possession of the applicant and other co-accused persons 10 quintal prohibited thai mangur fish was recovered.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that although entire allegations made against the applicant are totally false and baseless but even if entire allegations are accepted then also as there is no allegation of any adulteration, therefore, implication of the applicant under section 272 IPC is bad. It is further submitted that as far as offences under section 188 IPC and offences under the provisions of Food Safety Acts are concerned both are non cognizable offences. He further Sameer Khan And Another vs State Of U.P. on 27 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156936203/ 1 submitted that applicants are having no criminal history and they are in jail in the present matter since 28.12.2022, therefore, they may be released on bail. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the fact that there is no allegation against the applicants that they adulterated any food item and only allegation against them is that from their possession thai mangur fish was recovered which was prohibited one.
texts.petitioner_arguments: Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that although entire allegations made against the applicant are totally false and baseless but even if entire allegations are accepted then also as there is no allegation of any adulteration, therefore, implication of the applicant under section 272 IPC is bad. It is further submitted that as far as offences under section 188 IPC and offences under the provisions of Food Safety Acts are concerned both are non cognizable offences. He further Sameer Khan And Another vs State Of U.P. on 27 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156936203/ 1 submitted that applicants are having no criminal history and they are in jail in the present matter since 28.12.2022, therefore, they may be released on bail. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the fact that there is no allegation against the applicants that they adulterated any food item and only allegation against them is that from their possession thai mangur fish was recovered which was prohibited one.
